open_errors.issue: Dhanu says 'I told my sister he'd lose you on the Stair' and at once bellows for Gauri, so the reader takes Gauri for his sister. Everywhere else in the book Gauri is Dhanu's wife and Mini's mother (ch 19 'his wife', ch 26 'my keeper's widow', ch 28).

patches.find: You're the surveyor. I told my sister he'd lose you on the Stair.
patches.replace: You're the surveyor. I told my wife he'd lose you on the Stair.

open_errors.issue: Kunal took Ila's lie-cold in ch 15 and knows she lied about her orders. In ch 22 he calls her the one person who has never lied to his face, and in ch 24 his own POV calls her a surveyor who had never lied to him.
open_errors.fix: Acknowledge the single lie he took and that she confessed it at dawn.

patches.find: All that's left to argue about is whether the one person on this mountain who's never lied to my face gets the true line, or whether Raghu draws a bad one and sells it.
patches.replace: All that's left to argue about is whether the one person on this mountain who lied to my face once and owned it by dawn gets the true line, or whether Raghu draws a bad one and sells it.

patches.find: He had his dead fingertips and a surveyor who had never lied to him.
patches.replace: He had his dead fingertips and a surveyor who had lied to him once, and told him so by dawn.

open_errors.issue: Ch 17 fixes the storm's third day as day twenty of the bond, which makes the Mirror crossing (ch 13 to 14) about day seventeen. Yet ch 13 says six days roped together, and ch 14 and ch 15 say she has carried the letter (received before the binding) six days. Ch 20, the night after day twenty, says 'nine days' twice.
open_errors.fix: Bring the elapsed-time remarks into line with the day-twenty count.

patches.find: He had watched her work for six days now and it had not once grown ordinary.
patches.replace: He had watched her work for more than two weeks now and it had not once grown ordinary.

patches.find: She had carried it for six days. She knew every thread of the stitching that held it.
patches.replace: She had carried it for more than two weeks. She knew every thread of the stitching that held it.

patches.find: I don't know why she wants the lakes. I've carried it six days and haven't opened it.
patches.replace: I don't know why she wants the lakes. I've carried it more than two weeks and haven't opened it.

patches.find: It was one of the things he had noticed about her in nine days: she waited like a woman holding a level, to see which way the bubble went.
patches.replace: It was one of the things he had noticed about her in twenty days: she waited like a woman holding a level, to see which way the bubble went.

patches.find: Whatever it was, she had carried it nine days.
patches.replace: Whatever it was, she had carried it three weeks.

open_errors.issue: The timing of the ridge episode varies. Ch 20 and ch 28 say Kunal's father died at the end of summer, Pritam told the Udai story at supper a week after the funeral, and the Kuhl ridge came a month after, in autumn. Ch 11 says the father died 'that winter' and the ridge came a week after the funeral. Ch 13 and ch 17 put the supper 'the winter' Kunal was nine.
open_errors.fix: End of summer for the death, a month for the ridge, autumn for the supper.

patches.find: "My father died that winter," said Kunal.
patches.replace: "My father died at the end of that summer," said Kunal.

patches.find: My uncle was his younger brother, and he came to the funeral, and a week after it he took me up a ridge above the house.
patches.replace: My uncle was his younger brother, and he came to the funeral, and a month after it he took me up a ridge above the house.

patches.find: He thought of his uncle, who had taught him the winter he was nine, over supper, in the pleasant voice he used for terrible things.
patches.replace: He thought of his uncle, who had taught him the autumn he was nine, over supper, in the pleasant voice he used for terrible things.

patches.find: He said it at supper, the winter I was nine. My father was a week in the ground.
patches.replace: He said it at supper, the autumn I was nine. My father was a week in the ground.

open_errors.issue: Ch 2 and ch 31 place the spring council at the Shilak Cairn on Shilak's thaw day, which comes on day 56. Ch 17 says the council date is thirty-five days off (thirty-five is the Meadow Cairn's bond clock), and ch 22 says the council sits at Garh Neshar.
open_errors.fix: Make the thirty-five-day count the Meadow Cairn's, and seat the council at the Shilak Cairn.

patches.find: He had started it the night the hill council fixed the date at Garh Neshar, thirty-five days to Shilak's thaw council, when the crown's men and the hill's would sit down at one table and read what had been written.
patches.replace: He had started it the night of the binding, thirty-five days to the Meadow Cairn's meltwater in a soft year, with Shilak's thaw council somewhere after, when the crown's men and the hill's would sit down at one table and read what had been written.

patches.find: When the thaw council sits at Garh Neshar, I stand up and ask two things of the crown.
patches.replace: When the thaw council sits at the Shilak Cairn, I stand up and ask two things of the crown.

open_errors.issue: Ila recalls Kunal's Udai story as said 'by the fire three nights ago'. He told it at the toppled door cairn on the Hollow Moon in ch 10, several nights and a storm earlier, and there was no fire.
open_errors.fix: Place the memory at the door cairn.

patches.find: and she thought of the thing he had said by the fire three nights ago, as lightly as he might say the time.
patches.replace: and she thought of the thing he had said at the broken door cairn on the Hollow Moon, as lightly as he might say the time.

open_errors.issue: 'Every warden hanged since for crossing a pass': under the Closing Law smugglers hang, while wardens enforce it and die chasing them.

patches.find: Every warden hanged since for crossing a pass in the cold.
patches.replace: Every smuggler hanged since for crossing a pass in the cold.

open_errors.issue: Ila calls 410 of her paces 'a third' of a mile. Ch 13 has 910 of her paces as a third of a mile, so 410 is nearer a seventh.

patches.find: It's a third, and the third is mine to say.
patches.replace: It's nearer a seventh, and the seventh is mine to say.

open_errors.issue: Ch 12 says the Ladder is the first line she ever left out on purpose and that she had 'not decided about' the east bearing. Ch 3 and ch 32 state that she left the east bearing out deliberately, by choice.
open_errors.fix: Make the Ladder the first omission she owns aloud, not the first deliberate one.

patches.find: It was the first line she had ever left out on purpose and then known she had left out. The one on the east, in the dark, she had followed him past and not decided about. This one she decided.
patches.replace: It was the first line she had ever left out on purpose and meant to say so aloud. The one on the east, in the dark, she had left off in silence. This one she would own.

open_errors.issue: The queen's letter was sewn in Ila's coat lining from ch 3 and moved to her pattu hem only in ch 20. Ch 21 says it has been in her hem 'since the Stair', and ch 26 says 'in your hem for a week'.
open_errors.fix: Refer to it as sewn into her since the Fair.

patches.find: Your letter has been in your hem since the Stair, and it came from the crown's drawer.
patches.replace: Your letter has been sewn into you since the Fair, and it came from the crown's drawer.

patches.find: You've carried that letter in your hem for a week and refused me twice, and now this.
patches.replace: You've carried that letter sewn into you since the Fair and refused me twice, and now this.

open_errors.issue: Kunal recalls the Drum soundings as 'two days ago'. They were made the morning she opened the letter (ch 15), before a multi-day storm and the visits to the Eye and the huts.
open_errors.fix: Replace the count with the event.

patches.find: He had stood at her shoulder on the Drum two days ago and watched her chip her holes with his own knife and the iron spike, tapping the haft, listening for the ring.
patches.replace: He had stood at her shoulder on the Drum, the morning she opened the letter, and watched her chip her holes with his own knife and the iron spike, tapping the haft, listening for the ring.

open_errors.issue: In ch 7 Ila only measured Gauri's pen wall and advised a footing course, and Gauri said she would lay it. Gauri left the next noon and now stays at the lake huts. Ch 28 has Ila putting the course under 'the lambing wall at Ewe's Rest'. The lambing wall is the half-ring on the plateau, not the pen.
open_errors.fix: Make it the pen wall, and Ila's finding rather than her work.

patches.find: "The lambing wall at Ewe's Rest," he said. "Ila put a flat-stone course under the north side. It'll hold this spring."
patches.replace: "The pen wall at Ewe's Rest," he said. "Ila showed you where the north side was short. Footed, it'll hold this spring."

open_errors.issue: Ila says that at the Meadow Cairn, the first night, she let the chill build 'rather than follow you east'. The east line appeared at a roadside cairn up the Neshar road, and in ch 3 she did follow him east after letting the chill build.
open_errors.fix: Correct the place and the outcome.

patches.find: At the Meadow Cairn, the first night, I stood eight spans and a bit from you, and I let the rope chill my wrists to the elbow rather than follow you east.
patches.replace: On the Neshar road, the first night, I stood eight spans and a bit from you, and I let the rope chill my wrists to the elbow before I'd follow you east.

open_errors.issue: Kunal recalls that Ila refused him a promise 'on the ledge'. The refusal in ch 12 took place at the hearth niche at the Ladder's foot.

patches.find: But she had refused him a promise on the ledge because she would not give one she might break
patches.replace: But she had refused him a promise at the Ladder's foot because she would not give one she might break
